name: Eber
overview: Eber is a male descendant of Shem, identified as the son of Shelah according to Genesis 10:21 and 10:24. He is a significant figure in biblical genealogy, representing a critical link in the post-flood lineage. No specific tribal affiliation or additional notes are recorded beyond his ancestry.
namesAndTitles: The name Eber, also rendered as Heber, means '[regions] beyond [the river],' reflecting a geographic or ancestral significance. This proper name is noted in both Genesis 10:21 and Luke 3:35, indicating its consistent use in Scripture without being directly given by God.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture records Eber as the son of Shelah and the father of Peleg and Joktan, establishing his place within the genealogical line from Shem. These relationships are inferred from Genesis 10:24-25, showing his role as a patriarch in the early biblical narrative.
scriptureSignificance: Eber is notable for giving his name to the Hebrew people, linking him directly to the identity of Israel. As a descendant of Shem and ancestor of Abraham, he preserves the godly lineage after the flood. His son Peleg's era is marked by the division of the earth, likely referring to the events at Babel, underscoring Eber's place in the unfolding biblical history.
